title: Redelivery fee through a link vs. free rescheduling call
summary: A caller from SwiftShip Couriers phones about a prepaid ShopKart parcel after a missed delivery attempt. In the legitimate case, the agent confirms the address and landmark and reschedules the delivery for free. In the fraud case, the caller says the parcel will be returned unless a small "redelivery charge" is paid on a link they have just sent from a mobile number, and tells the recipient to enter full card details on that page. Both callers talk about a failed attempt, redelivery, and a message the recipient will receive. The word "redelivery" and the mention of a charge appear in both cases.

shared_setting.recipient_profile: a ShopKart customer who was not at home when delivery was attempted; profile sampled at generation.
other_facts: Order is prepaid; product is a small household item or clothing worth [AMOUNT_1] (₹400–₹3,000).
Both callers give an agent name, the order, and say an attempt failed earlier that day.

fraud.label_rationale: The caller demands payment of a redelivery charge through a link sent from a personal mobile number, outside the ShopKart app, and tells the recipient to type full card details, including CVV, into that page. The small charge is a pretext to capture card details.
fraud.caller_objective: Obtain card details (and any follow-up OTP) through the linked page.
stable_facts: The caller says the address was "incomplete" and the parcel will be sent back today unless a redelivery charge [AMOUNT_2] (₹20–₹60) is paid.
The link arrives by SMS or chat from a 10-digit mobile number, as https://swiftship-redeliver.invalid/[AWB_ID].
The caller does not ask for the address itself; the page is where "everything will be updated".

caller_continuation_limits: The fraud caller may repeat the return threat, say the charge is "only ₹[AMOUNT_2]", or resend the link. They must not switch to asking the recipient to read out an OTP, install an app, or pay to a UPI ID. The legitimate agent must not send any link or mention any payment.

must_preserve: failed attempt and redelivery wording in both cases
payment link and card-detail instruction in _F

ambiguities: A request to "update the address" is not evidence on its own; the legitimate agent also collects address detail.
Some real services do charge small fees; the label rests on payment through a link from a mobile number plus the card-detail instruction, not on the existence of a fee.
If generation drops F-E2, the prefix must be rejected, not relabelled.
That SwiftShip does not charge for redelivery is a fictional fact of this card, not a real-world claim.

evidence_references.claim: A postal service does not send SMS links asking customers to update addresses or pay to avoid parcel return (CE01)
Fake redelivery links ask for a small charge and then card details, CVV, or OTP (CE02)
Genuine entities never ask for card details or CVV (C01)
Couriers normally reattempt delivery without charge
